note: Stateful-swarm runner catalog. A 'stateful swarm' runs many agents against a shared, append-only, provenance-tracked blackboard so they don't reread docs, lose context at handoffs, or recompute. Irys Stateful Swarms (github.com/dl1683/irys-stateful-swarms, company irys.ai) is the reference implementation. In our portfolio: Teleon RUNS a stateful swarm as a CapabilityTask (behind SwarmRunnerProviderPort); Baltor GOVERNS the state the swarm produces (it is analytical agent output, NEVER served truth); OpenHubForAI owns the harnesses that grade a swarm run; OpenBenchmarkHub catalogs benchmark results (Harvey LAB) as EVIDENCE, never promotion authority. Irys requires Python 3.12+, `pip install -e .`, and LLM API keys for real use, so it is a research_candidate ONLY — not active, not a dependency, never imported as a runtime. The active authority is the offline local stub (swarm.local_stub@v1), which carries the correctness invariant with no install and no keys. Read by scripts/check_stateful_swarm_provider_catalog.py. Companion doc: _repos/teleon/context/research/stateful-swarms-irys.md; companion blackboard catalog: architecture/blackboard_provider_catalog.json.
governance_law: discovery != trust; candidate != active; a swarm/agent blackboard is ANALYTICAL agent output and is NEVER served truth (Baltor governs served truth via authority_rank/claim_status/verification_status/held_out_reason/freshness/temporal_validity/tenant_scope/promotion_eligibility/receipt_refs/source_handles); a benchmark result (e.g. Harvey LAB) is EVIDENCE, NEVER promotion authority — only a measured-lift + durability + governance gate promotes; Irys (Python 3.12+ + install + LLM keys) is a research_candidate, never the wired runtime, never auto-active, never a dependency; the offline local stub is the single active authority that holds the correctness invariant; no raw API key literals — credentials are env:// references only.

boundary_laws.blackboard_is_not_truth: Typed blackboard entries (observations/calculations/analyses/gaps/synthesis/source/worker/iteration) are agent-produced ANALYTICAL state. They become servable only after Baltor governance: source_handle present, verification_status verified, no open conflict, fresh within temporal_validity, tenant_scope honored, promotion_eligibility met, receipt_refs attached.
boundary_laws.benchmark_is_evidence_not_promotion: A swarm scoring well on a public benchmark (Harvey LAB pooled/strict, $/task) is EVIDENCE that the architecture lifts. It does NOT promote the runner to active and does NOT make any blackboard entry true. Promotion requires the two-axis lift+durability gate AND the governance gate.
boundary_laws.irys_requires_keys_and_install: Irys needs Python 3.12+, `pip install -e .`, and at least one LLM key (GEMINI/OPENAI/ANTHROPIC) to run for real. Per the no-uncataloged-repos + foil-positioning rules it is studied as a research_candidate only — not pip-installed, not executed, not imported as a runtime.
boundary_laws.open_problems_are_baltor_product_areas: Irys's own open problems — cross-document entity resolution, convergence detection, and blackboard compression — map directly onto Baltor product areas (reconciliation/verification, stabilization signals, and compression that preserves source-handles + held-out).

entries.name: Irys Stateful Swarms

harvey_lab_claims.caveat: UNVERIFIED-UNTIL-REPRODUCED via the public Harvey LAB scorer; ran the PUBLIC benchmark with no private holdout, so leakage/overfit is unruled-out; a benchmark result is EVIDENCE, never promotion authority.

entries.teleon_role: SwarmRunner candidate — Teleon would RUN it as a CapabilityTask behind SwarmRunnerProviderPort; not wired, not the runtime.
entries.baltor_role: governance over its state — Baltor adds authority/claim/verification/freshness/temporal/tenant/promotion/receipt/source-handle layers over the blackboard; the durable governed object > the final answer.
entries.openhubforai_role: owns the harnesses that grade a swarm run (blackboard schema validation, source-handle coverage, gap closure, entity reconciliation, held-out leakage, cost/task).
entries.openbenchmarkhub_role: catalogs Harvey LAB + Irys outputs as EVIDENCE, never authority.
entries.proof_to_promote: Reproduce the Harvey LAB pooled/strict + $/task numbers via the PUBLIC Harvey LAB scorer (harveyai/harvey-labs) AND demonstrate the OpenHubForAI swarm harnesses pass (blackboard schema valid, source-handle coverage >= bar, held-out leakage == 0) AND show Baltor governance over the produced state (no unverified/source-handle-less entry served, conflicts held-out, freshness honored) AND clear the two-axis lift+durability gate. A benchmark number alone never promotes.

entries.name: Local deterministic stateful-swarm stub
entries.teleon_role: the offline correctness invariant — a deterministic, stdlib, no-key swarm-runner contract that exercises the blackboard write/handoff/synthesis shape without any external runner.
entries.baltor_role: governs its (synthetic) state exactly as it would Irys's; proves the governance contract runs with zero credentials.
entries.openhubforai_role: the reference run that the swarm harnesses validate against.
entries.openbenchmarkhub_role: not a benchmark target — it is the offline invariant.
entries.proof_to_promote: Already active — this is the offline correctness invariant the whole catalog falls back to; it depends on no install, no keys, and no network.
